children: Credit Acceptance agreed to pay $75.5 million to resolve allegations from attorneys general that it gave predatory loans to low-income consumers.

The auto lending company said Thursday it entered consent judgements with 41 attorneys general to resolve litigation brought against the company in 2023. The settlement was reached without any admission of wrongdoing, the company said.

Credit Acceptance will pay $60 million to a consumer relief fund and $15.5 million to the participating attorneys general for their investigation. It will also provide debt relief in the form of a waiver of all outstanding balances to certain customers.

Credit Acceptance funds and services car loans for subprime and deep subprime consumers. New York Attorney General Letitia James filed a lawsuit in January 2023 claiming the company engaged in deceptive and abusive acts by offering loans with exorbitant interest rates and add-on products.
The company offered interest rates around 22%, which is at or near the maximum rate allowed in many states, the lawsuit alleged.
The settlement will not require Credit Acceptance to record additional charges beyond those already accrued and disclosed in financial statements, the company said.
